指甲的坏习惯，这时，

第一时间的启蒙书

[P4] 贝贝熊系列丛书
The Berenstain Bears
and the
坏习惯
BAD HABIT
（美）斯坦·博丹 简·博丹 绘著
Stan & Jan Berenstain
张德启等 译
父母和孩子一起阅读
家长和子女共同成长

[P5] 小熊妹妹上学已经有一段时间了。她和熊爸爸、熊妈妈、小熊哥哥一起住在熊王国的一座大树屋里，门前有一条金色的土路，通往熊王国深处。

小熊妹妹最早上的是宝宝班，在那里，几乎全是玩：玩洋娃娃、摆积木、做泥蛇、用蜡笔随便画画。

[P6] 接下来上幼儿园，那儿也挺有意思：练队列、参加鼓乐队，还学了好多数字，字母也差不多学全了。

[P7] 现在，小熊妹妹上一年级了。上学的确跟以前不一样，在学校里，虽然还是能和小朋友一起玩，她也很喜欢老师简，但除了玩，还要学好多好多新东西：拼写、算术和其他功课。

帽子
蝙蝠
猫
球
香肠
3+4=7
2+5=7

上/下
大/小
外/里

[P8] 在教室里，必须全神贯注。有时候，精力太集中了，就会让孩子们紧张，慢慢养成了一些坏习惯。
在老师简的班里，就发生了这样的事：

丽兹用手卷头发，卷呀，卷呀，不停地卷。

弗雷德用手挠头，挠呀，挠呀，不停地挠。

诺曼用嘴吮拇指，吮呀，吮呀，不停地吮。

而小熊妹妹则咬手指甲，咬呀，咬呀，不停地咬。

[P9] 不知不觉，手指甲已经被她咬得只剩下一小片了。实际上，指甲已被咬得实在太秃了，有些手指开始疼起来了。

[P10] 一天，小熊妹妹放学回到家，熊妈妈看见了她的手指，“天哪！你把指甲咬得只剩一小片了。瞧，已经完全秃了，怎么回事呀？
小熊妹妹说：‘妈妈，我也不知道怎么回事，有几个手指头好疼呀！’

[P11] 熊妈妈说：“嗯，这样吧，在疼的手指上抹点儿药，把所有的手指头缠上胶布。胶布会提醒你不再咬指甲，也可以让指甲尽快再长出来。”

[P12] 手指尖上缠满了胶布，小熊妹妹真不咬指甲了，但做事却不方便了：
握钢笔费劲了，
选频道不灵活了，
挠痒痒也挠不痛快了，
就连抓石子一次
也只能抓两个……

[P14] 最糟糕的是：那些胶布
仿佛在告诉全世界，小熊妹妹是个爱咬指甲的孩子。

[P15] 第二天早晨，小熊妹妹排着队去上学，丽兹和其他几个孩子指着小熊妹妹开玩笑：“小熊妹妹，咬指甲！小熊妹妹，咬指甲！”小熊妹妹再也忍不住了，把胶布一古脑儿全扒了下来。

[P16] 没有了胶布，她忘了不能咬指甲。
上课在咬。
坐车也在咬。
和小熊哥哥一起
下车，还在咬。

[P17] 小熊哥哥说：“妹妹，你得改掉这个坏毛病。不然，你就会一天到晚咬个不停了。”

[P18] “小熊哥哥说得对。不是我爱唠叨，但咬指甲确实是个不好改的习惯。”熊妈妈边说边往手推车上装着种花的东西。
“习惯？什么叫习惯？”小熊妹妹捏紧拳头，不让咬得光秃秃的手指露出来。

[P19] 熊妈妈说：“这个问题问得好。跟我来，我要把奶奶送来的郁金香种子种上，咱们边走边说。”

[P20] 熊妈妈推着手推车，沿着深深的车轮印儿走着，说：“习惯，就是你连想也不用想就经常做的事。习惯是生活中很重要的一部分。大部分习惯都是好的，像早晨起床后刷牙、梳头、过马路前往两边看看……但有些习惯就不那么好了。”
小熊妹妹问：“像咬手指甲？”
熊妈妈说：“对。你一定想让你的指甲长回到原来漂亮的样子，是不是呀？”
小熊妹妹说：“当然啦！可我老忘记！为什么总是记不住呢？”

[P21] 熊妈妈说：“嗯，这有点儿像这条小路。我推着小车走在这条路上好多次了，中间已经压出一道深深的槽。而且，我每走一次，这道槽还在加深。瞧，现在已经深得要靠人帮忙才能把车拉出来。”

[P22] “坏习惯也是这样，时间越长，就越难改掉。到了，郁金香就种在这儿。”
“那我咬指甲的习惯怎么办呢？”小熊妹妹边说边帮妈妈把车子从深深的槽里拉出来，“怎样才能改掉这个坏习惯呢？”

[P23] 熊妈妈说：“你只是需要一点儿帮助就行。来，咱们边种郁金香边想办法。过一会儿，我去找你爸爸，或许他也能出些主意。”

[P24] 熊爸爸建议说：“我可以把坏毛病惩罚办法读给她听。听着：咬指甲是最粗俗、最丢人的坏习惯，如果不立即改掉……”
熊妈妈说：“天哪，别这样！咬指甲是紧张导致的一种习惯。喊叫和吓唬只能使她更紧张。”
熊爸爸若有所思地说：“可能是吧。也许，奖励能起到作用。奖励钱……比如，每天不咬指甲就奖励一角。”

[P25] 小熊妹妹一直在隔壁紧张地咬着指甲，熊爸爸话音刚落，她就一下子蹦了进来，“一角——每天不咬指甲就奖励我整整十分钱？”
熊爸爸说：“对，直到你改掉这个毛病！”

想着就要到手的那些可爱的钱币，她下了决心：“我再也不咬指甲了！”

[P26] 可结果是，她一角钱也没得到，到头来，只是更加灰心丧气了。
一天太长，而且，习惯也太顽固了。特别是坏习惯。即使有一角钱的奖励，小熊妹妹也记不住不咬指甲。熊爸爸、熊妈妈也很沮丧。

[P27] 熊妈妈叹了口气：“唉，日子还得过。我得给奶奶打个电话，谢谢她送的郁金香种子。”

[P28] 奶奶接了电话，说：“噢，亲爱的，别客气。家里都好吗？……是吗？……听着，我小时候也爱咬指甲，是我妈妈帮我改掉的。你都试了哪些办法？嗯……嗯……，我想你们奖励她钱是对的。但不要一天一角，也不要一天过完了才奖给她……”

听了奶奶的高招，熊妈妈感叹道：“这个主意太好了！”，

[P29] 他们按照奶奶的办法做，每天早晨给小熊妹妹十分钱——每个指甲一分。只要不咬指甲，她就可以保留那十分钱。

口袋里装着这些硬币，

上车的时候，叮叮当当……

跳绳的时候，叮叮当当……

[P30] 刚想咬指甲，"叮叮当当"的声音又在耳边响起来……

这一招真的奏效了！

但还不是完全有效，改掉一个
坏习惯真是不容易，小熊妹妹有时
不得不还回去几枚硬币。但在十天
里，她还是存下了九十三枚硬币！

[P31] 更棒的是，她有了
十个漂亮的手指甲！

捡东西很自如，

调频道很灵活，

挠痒痒很痛快。

[P32] 抓石子，她一下子抓了十个！
熊爸爸高兴地说：“感谢上帝！坏习惯终于
改掉了。”
“是啊，太好了！”熊妈妈也长舒了一口气。
这时，小熊哥哥看着自己的手指甲叫了起来：
“听着，我也要开始咬指甲！这样，我就也有
钱花了！”

[P33] 熊爸爸大声吼道：“开什么玩笑！如果你敢……”
小熊哥哥赶紧说：“开玩笑，开玩笑！”
他也只能开开玩笑罢了。

[P34] The Berenstain Bears
and the BAD HABIT
When cubs start to twitch or to scratch or to nibble,
what they need is some help, not a lecture or quibble.

1. Sister Bear, who lived with her mama, papa, and brother in the big tree house down a sunny
dirt road deep in Bear Country, had been going to school for quite a while.

First there had been nursery school, which was pure fun—playing with dolls and blocks, rolling clay snakes, and scribbling with crayons.

Next had come kindergarten. That was fun too. There were marching games and rhythm band.
She also learned a lot of numbers in kindergarten—and most of the alphabet.

2. Now Sister was in first grade. Regular school was different. It was still fun and she liked
Teacher Jane very much, but it wasn’t all fun. There was quite a lot of work—spelling, number
problems, all kinds of things.

In regular school you have to concentrate—and sometimes when you concentrate, you form
little nervous habits. That’s what happened to some of the cubs in Teacher Jane’s class.

Lizzy twirled her fur.
Twirl, twirl, twirl.

Freddy scratched his head
Scratch, scratch, scratch.

Norman sucked his thumb.
Suck, suck, suck.

And Sister nibbled her nails.
Nibble, nibble, nibble.

3. Before she knew it, she had nibbled them down to nubbins. In fact, she nibbled them down so
far that some of her fingers were getting sore.

[P35] "Oh, dear!" said Mama Bear to Sister when the cubs got home from school one day. "You've nibbled your nails down to nubbins. In fact, you've nibbled them clean off. How did it happen?"
4. "Hmm," said Mama. "Well, here's what we'll do. We'll put a little medicine on the sore ones and bits of adhesive tape on all of them. That will remind you not to nibble and will give them a chance to grow back."

The bits of tape helped Sister remember not to nibble, but they also got in the way when she tried to do certain things. It's very hard to hold a pencil with tape all over your fingertips,
or tune the TV,
or scratch when you have an itch.

And when Sister tried to play jacks, she couldn't get any higher than twosies.

5. But worst of all, the bits of tape told the whole world that Sister Bear was a nail biter.

6. The next morning, when Sister lined up for school, Lizzy Bruin and some others began pointing and teasing: "Sister nibbles her nails! Sister nibbles her nails!" It didn't take Sister long to decide to pull off those bits of tape!

And without the tape, she forgot to remember not to nibble.

She forgot during school.

She forgot on the bus.

She even forgot as she and Brother climbed off the bus.

7. "You're going to have to cut that out, Sis," said Brother, "or you'll get to be a regular full-time nail biter."

"I'm afraid your brother's right," said Mama, who was organizing the wheelbarrow for some garden work. "I don't mean to nag, but nail biting is a very difficult habit to break."

"Habit?" asked Sister, making fists so that her nubby, nibbled-off nails wouldn't show. "What's a habit?"

8. "That's a good question," said Mama. "Come along while I plant these tulip bulbs Grizzly Gran sent over and we'll talk about it."

[P36] "A habit," Mama said as she pushed the wheelbarrow along the well-worn path. "is something you do so often you don't even have to think about it. Habits are a very important part of our lives. And most of them are good—like brushing your teeth and combing your fur when you get up in the morning, and looking both ways before you cross a road. But some habits aren't so good." 
"Like nail biting?" asked Sister. 
"You would like to have your nice nails grow back, wouldn't you?" was Mama's answer. 
"Oh, yes!" said Sister. "But I keep forgetting! Why is it so hard to remember?" 
9. "Well," said Mama, "it's sort of like this path. I've wheeled this barrow over it so many times that it's worn a deep rut right down the middle. And it keeps getting deeper every time I use it. Why, it's so deep now that I can't get out of it without a little help. 
"That's the way it is with a bad habit—the more you use it, the harder it is to get out of it. Here, this is where I want to plant the bulbs." 
"What about my nail-biting habit?" asked Sister as she helped Mama out of the deep rut. "How am I going to get out of it?" 
10. "You just need a little help, that's all," said Mama. "Let's plant Gran's tulips while I think about it. And later I'll talk to your papa. He may have some ideas. " 
"I could read the riot act to her," suggested Papa. "You know: 'Nail biting is an outrageous, disgraceful habit and if you don't stop it immediately—' " 
"Dear me, no!" said Mama. "Nail biting is a kind of nervous habit, and shouting and threatening will just make her more nervous." 
"I suppose so," said Papa thoughtfully. "Perhaps some sort of reward would help. A bit of money—let's say a dime for every day she doesn't bite her nails." 
11. Before Mama could answer, Sister Bear, who had been nervously nibbling in the next room, popped in and said, "A dime—ten whole cents every day just for not biting my nails?" 
"That's right," said Papa. "Until the habit's broken." 
"I'll never nibble again!" she said as she thought of all those lovely dimes she was going to get. But the way it turned out, she didn't get a single dime. All she got was discouraged.

[P37] A day is a long time and habits are powerful—especially bad habits. Even with the promise of a dime, Sister couldn’t remember not to nibble. Mama and Papa got discouraged too.
12. "Oh, well," sighed Mama. "Life goes on. I must call Gran and thank her for the tulip bulbs."
"Oh, you’re very welcome, my dear," said Gran when Mama called. "And how is everything at your house?...Is that so?...You know, I was a nail biter when I was a cub and my mama helped me to stop. What have you tried so far?...Um...Uh-huh... Well, I think you’re on the right track with the dime, but instead of a dime, and instead of giving it to her at the end of the day..."
"What an interesting idea," said Mama as she listened to wise old Grizzly Gran.
13. So they tried Gran’s idea. Instead of a dime at the end of each day, they gave Sister ten pennies—one for each nail—at the beginning of each day. Ten pennies to keep—unless she nibbled.
And with those pennies in her pocket,
jiggling when she got on the school bus,
jingling when she jumped rope in the schoolyard...
...just waiting to be remembered when some nail decided it needed a nibble...
the plan worked!
Not perfectly. It’s hard to break a habit, and Sister had to give back some of those pennies. But in ten days she had ninety-three pennies!
14. But even better: she had ten fine fingernails.
Great for picking things up,
tuning the TV,
and scratching itches.
And the next time she played jacks she got all the way to tensies!
"Phew!" said Papa Bear. "I’m glad that’s over."
"Yes, indeed!" agreed Mama, breathing a great sigh of relief.
That’s when Brother Bear looked at his fingernails and piped up, "You know, I think I might start biting my nails—I could use the money."
15. "I certainly hope you’re joking!" roared Papa. "Because if you’re not—"
"I’m joking. I’m joking," interrupted Brother.
And he was—sort of.

[P2] The Berenstain Bears

Bad Habit
When children develop bad habits like picking, scratching, and biting their nails, what they need is help, not lectures or nagging.
An early启蒙 book

[P4] Berenstain Bears Series
The Berenstain Bears
and the
Bad Habit
BAD HABIT
(US) Stan & Jan Berenstain, Authors and Illustrators
Stan & Jan Berenstain
Translated by Zhang Deqi et al.
Parents and children read together
Parents and children grow together

[P5] Little Bear Sister has been going to school for some time now. She lives with Bear Dad, Bear Mom, and her brother in a big treehouse in Bear Kingdom, with a golden dirt road in front leading deep into the kingdom.

Little Bear Sister started in the baby class, where they mostly played: playing with dolls, building blocks, making mud snakes, and drawing freely with crayons.

[P6] Next came kindergarten, which was also quite fun: practicing lines, joining the drum band, learning lots of numbers, and almost mastering all the letters.

[P7] Now, Little Bear Sister is in first grade. Going to school is really different from before. At school, she can still play with her friends, and she really likes her teacher, Jane. But besides playing, she has to learn lots and lots of new things: spelling, arithmetic, and other subjects.

Hat
Bat
Cat
Ball
Sausage
3+4=7
2+5=7

Up/Down
Big/Small
Outside/Inside

[P8] In the classroom, you must be fully focused. Sometimes, when children are too focused, they get tense and slowly develop some bad habits.
In Teacher Jane's class, this happened:

Liz twirls her hair with her hand, twirling, twirling, never stopping.

Fred scratches his head with his hand, scratching, scratching, never stopping.

Norman sucks his thumb with his mouth, sucking, sucking, never stopping.

And Little Bear Sister bites her fingernails, biting, biting, never stopping.

[P9] Unknowingly, her fingernails had been bitten down to just small pieces. In fact, the nails had been bitten so short that some fingers began to hurt.

[P10] One day, after school, Little Bear Sister came home. Bear Mom saw her fingers and said, "Goodness! You've bitten your nails down to just a tiny bit. Look, they're completely bare. What's going on?"
Little Bear Sister said, "Mom, I don't know what's happening. A few of my fingers really hurt!"

[P11] Bear Mom said, "Well, here's what we'll do: put some medicine on the sore finger, and wrap all your fingertips with bandages. The bandages will remind you not to bite your nails, and they'll also help your nails grow back quickly."

[P12] With bandages wrapped around her fingertips, Little Bear Sister really stopped biting her nails, but doing things became inconvenient:
Holding a pen was difficult,
Changing channels was not flexible,
Scratching itches wasn't fun anymore,
And even picking up pebbles, she could only grab two at a time……

[P14] The worst part was: those bandages
seemed to tell the whole world that Little Bear was a child who bit her nails.

[P15] The next morning, Little Bear was lining up to go to school. Lizzie and a few other kids pointed at Little Bear and teased, "Little Bear, biting nails! Little Bear, biting nails!" Little Bear couldn't stand it anymore and ripped off all the bandages in one go.

[P16] Without the bandage, she forgot she shouldn't bite her nails.
She was biting during class.
She was biting while riding the bus.
Together with her brother Bear, 
she was still biting when getting off the bus.

[P17] Little Bear Brother said, "Sister, you must get rid of this bad habit. Otherwise, you'll keep biting your nails all day and night."

[P18] "Big Brother Bear is right. I'm not nagging, but biting nails is indeed a hard habit to break," said Bear Mom, as she loaded gardening supplies onto the wheelbarrow.
"Habit? What's a habit?" Little Bear Sister clenched her fists, hiding her bitten-down fingers.

[P19] Bear Mom said, "This question is well-asked. Come with me, I'm going to plant the tulip seeds Grandma sent. Let's walk and talk as we go."

[P20] Bear Mom pushed her cart along the deep tire tracks, saying, “Habits are things you do often without even thinking. Habits are an important part of life. Most habits are good, like brushing your teeth and combing your hair after waking up, or looking both ways before crossing the street… but some habits aren’t so good.”
Little Bear Sister asked, “Like biting your fingernails?”
Bear Mom said, “Yes. You must want your nails to grow back to their pretty shape, right?”
Little Bear Sister said, “Of course! But I always forget! Why can’t I ever remember?”

[P21] Bear Mom said, "Hmm, this is a bit like this little path. I've pushed this cart along this path many times, and it has already pressed out a deep groove in the middle. And every time I walk it, the groove gets deeper. Look, it's now so deep that I need help to pull the cart out."

[P22] "Bad habits are the same— the longer they go on, the harder they are to change. Here we are, the tulips will be planted right here."
"Then what should I do about my nail-biting habit?" Little Bear sister asked, helping her mom pull the cart out of the deep groove, "How can I get rid of this bad habit?"

[P23] Bear Mom said, "You just need a little help. Come on, let's plant some tulips and think of a solution together. In a little while, I'll go find your dad—maybe he can come up with some ideas too."

[P24] Bear Dad suggested, "I can read her the punishment methods for bad habits. Listen: biting nails is the most vulgar, most shameful bad habit. If it's not changed immediately..."
Bear Mom said, "Goodness, no! Nail-biting is a habit caused by tension. Yelling and scaring will only make her more tense."
Bear Dad said thoughtfully, "Maybe. Perhaps rewards could work. Reward money... for example, a dime for every day she doesn't bite her nails."

[P25] Little Bear was biting her nails nervously in the next room. As soon as Mr. Bear finished speaking, she jumped in, saying, "A dime—ten cents every day for not biting my nails?"
Mr. Bear said, "Yes, until you get rid of this habit!"

Thinking about the cute coins she was about to get, she made up her mind: "I'll never bite my nails again!"

[P26] But in the end, she didn't get a single cent, and only became more discouraged.
A day is too long, and habits are too stubborn, especially bad ones. Even with a ten-cent reward, Little Bear couldn't remember not to bite her nails. Bear Dad and Bear Mom were also very discouraged.

[P27] Bear Mom sighed, “Well, life goes on. I need to call Grandma and thank her for the tulip seeds she sent.”

[P28] Grandma answered the phone and said, “Oh, dear, don’t be shy. How’s everyone at home? …… Is that so? …… Listen, I used to bite my nails when I was little, and it was my mom who helped me break the habit. What methods have you tried? Hmm… hmm… I think rewarding her with money is the right approach. But don’t give her just one cent a day, and don’t wait until the day is over to give it to her…”

Having heard Grandma’s clever idea, Bear Mom exclaimed, “What a great idea!”,

[P29] They followed Grandma's advice. Every morning, they gave Little Bear Sister ten cents—one cent for each fingernail. As long as she didn't bite her nails, she could keep the ten cents.

With these coins in her pocket,

When getting on the bus, jingle jangle...

When jumping rope, jingle jangle...

[P30] Just as she was about to bite her nails, the "ding-dong" sound rang in her ears again...

This trick really worked!

But it wasn't completely effective. Breaking a bad habit is really hard. Sometimes, little bear sister had to give back a few coins. But in ten days, she still saved ninety-three coins!

[P31] The best part is, she has
 ten beautiful fingernails!

Picking things up is easy,

Changing channels is smooth,

Scratching itches is a breeze.

[P32] She grabbed ten pebbles at once!
Bear Dad happily said, “Thank God! The bad habit is finally
fixed.”
“Yes, wonderful!” Bear Mom also sighed in relief.
At that moment, Little Bear Brother looked at his fingernails and shouted:
“Listen, I want to start biting my nails too! That way, I’ll have
money to spend!”

[P33] Bear Dad shouted loudly, "What are you talking about! If you dare..."
Little Bear Brother quickly said, "Just kidding, just kidding!"
He could only joke around a little.

[P34] The Berenstain Bears
and the BAD HABIT
When cubs start to twitch or to scratch or to nibble,
what they need is some help, not a lecture or quibble.

1. Sister Bear, who lived with her mama, papa, and brother in the big tree house down a sunny
dirt road deep in Bear Country, had been going to school for quite a while.

First there had been nursery school, which was pure fun—playing with dolls and blocks, rolling clay snakes, and scribbling with crayons.

Next had come kindergarten. That was fun too. There were marching games and rhythm band.
She also learned a lot of numbers in kindergarten—and most of the alphabet.

2. Now Sister was in first grade. Regular school was different. It was still fun and she liked
Teacher Jane very much, but it wasn’t all fun. There was quite a lot of work—spelling, number
problems, all kinds of things.

In regular school you have to concentrate—and sometimes when you concentrate, you form
little nervous habits. That’s what happened to some of the cubs in Teacher Jane’s class.

Lizzy twirled her fur.
Twirl, twirl, twirl.

Freddy scratched his head
Scratch, scratch, scratch.

Norman sucked his thumb.
Suck, suck, suck.

And Sister nibbled her nails.
Nibble, nibble, nibble.

3. Before she knew it, she had nibbled them down to nubbins. In fact, she nibbled them down so
far that some of her fingers were getting sore.

[P35] "Oh, dear!" said Mama Bear to Sister when the cubs got home from school one day. "You've nibbled your nails down to nubbins. In fact, you've nibbled them clean off. How did it happen?"
4. "Hmm," said Mama. "Well, here's what we'll do. We'll put a little medicine on the sore ones and bits of adhesive tape on all of them. That will remind you not to nibble and will give them a chance to grow back."

The bits of tape helped Sister remember not to nibble, but they also got in the way when she tried to do certain things. It's very hard to hold a pencil with tape all over your fingertips,
or tune the TV,
or scratch when you have an itch.

And when Sister tried to play jacks, she couldn't get any higher than twosies.

5. But worst of all, the bits of tape told the whole world that Sister Bear was a nail biter.

6. The next morning, when Sister lined up for school, Lizzy Bruin and some others began pointing and teasing: "Sister nibbles her nails! Sister nibbles her nails!" It didn't take Sister long to decide to pull off those bits of tape!

And without the tape, she forgot to remember not to nibble.

She forgot during school.

She forgot on the bus.

She even forgot as she and Brother climbed off the bus.

7. "You're going to have to cut that out, Sis," said Brother, "or you'll get to be a regular full-time nail biter."

"I'm afraid your brother's right," said Mama, who was organizing the wheelbarrow for some garden work. "I don't mean to nag, but nail biting is a very difficult habit to break."

"Habit?" asked Sister, making fists so that her nubby, nibbled-off nails wouldn't show. "What's a habit?"

8. "That's a good question," said Mama. "Come along while I plant these tulip bulbs Grizzly Gran sent over and we'll talk about it."

[P36] "A habit," Mama said as she pushed the wheelbarrow along the well-worn path. "is something you do so often you don't even have to think about it. Habits are a very important part of our lives. And most of them are good—like brushing your teeth and combing your fur when you get up in the morning, and looking both ways before you cross a road. But some habits aren't so good." 
"Like nail biting?" asked Sister. 
"You would like to have your nice nails grow back, wouldn't you?" was Mama's answer. 
"Oh, yes!" said Sister. "But I keep forgetting! Why is it so hard to remember?" 
9. "Well," said Mama, "it's sort of like this path. I've wheeled this barrow over it so many times that it's worn a deep rut right down the middle. And it keeps getting deeper every time I use it. Why, it's so deep now that I can't get out of it without a little help. 
"That's the way it is with a bad habit—the more you use it, the harder it is to get out of it. Here, this is where I want to plant the bulbs." 
"What about my nail-biting habit?" asked Sister as she helped Mama out of the deep rut. "How am I going to get out of it?" 
10. "You just need a little help, that's all," said Mama. "Let's plant Gran's tulips while I think about it. And later I'll talk to your papa. He may have some ideas. " 
"I could read the riot act to her," suggested Papa. "You know: 'Nail biting is an outrageous, disgraceful habit and if you don't stop it immediately—' " 
"Dear me, no!" said Mama. "Nail biting is a kind of nervous habit, and shouting and threatening will just make her more nervous." 
"I suppose so," said Papa thoughtfully. "Perhaps some sort of reward would help. A bit of money—let's say a dime for every day she doesn't bite her nails." 
11. Before Mama could answer, Sister Bear, who had been nervously nibbling in the next room, popped in and said, "A dime—ten whole cents every day just for not biting my nails?" 
"That's right," said Papa. "Until the habit's broken." 
"I'll never nibble again!" she said as she thought of all those lovely dimes she was going to get. But the way it turned out, she didn't get a single dime. All she got was discouraged.

[P37] A day is a long time and habits are powerful—especially bad habits. Even with the promise of a dime, Sister couldn’t remember not to nibble. Mama and Papa got discouraged too.
12. "Oh, well," sighed Mama. "Life goes on. I must call Gran and thank her for the tulip bulbs."
"Oh, you’re very welcome, my dear," said Gran when Mama called. "And how is everything at your house?...Is that so?...You know, I was a nail biter when I was a cub and my mama helped me to stop. What have you tried so far?...Um...Uh-huh... Well, I think you’re on the right track with the dime, but instead of a dime, and instead of giving it to her at the end of the day..."
"What an interesting idea," said Mama as she listened to wise old Grizzly Gran.
13. So they tried Gran’s idea. Instead of a dime at the end of each day, they gave Sister ten pennies—one for each nail—at the beginning of each day. Ten pennies to keep—unless she nibbled.
And with those pennies in her pocket,
jiggling when she got on the school bus,
jingling when she jumped rope in the schoolyard...
...just waiting to be remembered when some nail decided it needed a nibble...
the plan worked!
Not perfectly. It’s hard to break a habit, and Sister had to give back some of those pennies. But in ten days she had ninety-three pennies!
14. But even better: she had ten fine fingernails.
Great for picking things up,
tuning the TV,
and scratching itches.
And the next time she played jacks she got all the way to tensies!
"Phew!" said Papa Bear. "I’m glad that’s over."
"Yes, indeed!" agreed Mama, breathing a great sigh of relief.
That’s when Brother Bear looked at his fingernails and piped up, "You know, I think I might start biting my nails—I could use the money."
15. "I certainly hope you’re joking!" roared Papa. "Because if you’re not—"
"I’m joking. I’m joking," interrupted Brother.
And he was—sort of.

[P1] 本页为《贝贝熊系列丛书》中《坏习惯》一书的封面，展示了熊爸爸、熊妈妈和两个小熊角色，以及书名、作者、译者和出版社等信息。
[P2] 本页为《贝贝熊系列丛书》中《坏习惯》一书的封面，展示了书名、英文标题、丛书名及一段关于帮助孩子改正坏习惯的说明文字，并配有插图。
[P3] 画面中，一只穿着粉色波点背带裤的小熊正走在小路上，周围有红色小鸟、蓝色鸟、绿色青蛙和一只蝴蝶，背景是一座树屋和绿色的田野，整体氛围活泼而自然。
[P4] 本页为《贝贝熊系列丛书》中《坏习惯》一书的封面，展示了书名、作者、译者及丛书名，并配有鼓励亲子共读的宣传语。
[P5] 本页介绍了小熊妹妹的家庭背景和她上学前在宝宝班的日常活动，画面展示了她在树屋前的院子里玩耍的场景。
[P6] 本页描绘了小熊妹妹在幼儿园的活动，包括排队、参加鼓乐队以及学习数字和字母，展现了她在幼儿园的快乐学习生活。
[P7] 小熊妹妹升入一年级，开始学习拼写、算术等新课程，画面展示了她在教室里上课的场景，黑板上写有汉字、算式和反义词。
[P8] 本页描述了在老师简的班级里，四个孩子因紧张而养成的不同坏习惯：丽兹卷头发、弗雷德挠头、诺曼吮拇指、小熊妹妹咬指甲，画面通过四个圆形插图分别展示了这些行为。
[P9] 小熊妹妹发现自己咬指甲的坏习惯导致指甲被咬得又短又疼，画面中她看着自己的手指，背景是校车驶向树屋的场景。
[P10] 小熊妹妹放学回家后，熊妈妈发现她咬坏了指甲，感到惊讶并询问原因，小熊妹妹表示自己也不知道，只觉得手指很疼。
[P11] 熊妈妈为小熊妹妹处理被咬伤的指甲，建议在手指上抹药并缠上胶布，以帮助指甲恢复并防止继续咬指甲。
[P12] 小熊妹妹的手指尖缠上胶布后，虽然不再咬指甲，但写字、换频道、挠痒和抓石子等日常活动都变得不方便，她感到困扰。
[P13] 画面描绘了小熊妹妹在树屋前的小路上行走，树桩上有两只青蛙在交谈，树枝上有三只小鸟，背景是粉色的树屋和楼梯，整体氛围宁静自然。
[P14] 小熊妹妹因咬指甲而缠上胶布，她觉得这让她在别人面前显得很尴尬，仿佛全世界都知道她的坏习惯。
[P15] 第二天早晨，小熊妹妹上学时被同学嘲笑咬指甲，她因感到尴尬和困扰，最终忍不住将手指上缠的胶布全部撕掉。
[P16] 小熊妹妹撕掉胶布后，又开始在上课、坐车和下车时咬指甲，完全忘记了之前的提醒。
[P17] 小熊哥哥劝告妹妹改掉咬指甲的坏习惯，否则会一直咬个不停。画面中，小熊哥哥在树屋前的花园里对妹妹说话，背景是粉色树屋和校车。
[P18] 熊妈妈在树屋前的花园里对小熊妹妹说咬指甲是个不好改的习惯，小熊妹妹则困惑地询问什么是习惯，并下意识地捏紧拳头藏起被咬伤的手指。
[P19] 熊妈妈推着装满园艺工具和种子的小车，带着小熊妹妹去种郁金香，并表示要边走边解释关于习惯的问题。
[P20] 熊妈妈在推着手推车散步时，向小熊妹妹解释什么是习惯，并举例说明好习惯与坏习惯的区别，小熊妹妹则困惑于自己为何总是忘记改掉咬指甲的习惯。
[P21] 熊妈妈推着装满园艺工具的小车，与小熊妹妹走在小路上，用小车压出的深槽比喻习惯的形成，解释习惯是如何在重复中不断加深的。
[P22] 熊妈妈和小熊妹妹在种郁金香的路上，熊妈妈解释坏习惯越久越难改，小熊妹妹则边帮妈妈拉车边询问如何改掉咬指甲的习惯。
[P23] 熊妈妈和小熊妹妹在花园里种郁金香，熊妈妈告诉妹妹只需要一点帮助就能改掉咬指甲的习惯，并计划去找熊爸爸一起想办法。
[P24] 熊爸爸提议用惩罚方式改正妹妹咬指甲的习惯，熊妈妈反对认为会加重紧张，熊爸爸随后提出用奖励金钱的方式鼓励改掉坏习惯。
[P25] 熊爸爸提出用金钱奖励的方式鼓励小熊妹妹改掉咬指甲的习惯，小熊妹妹被奖励吸引，下定决心不再咬指甲。
[P26] 小熊妹妹尝试用金钱奖励改掉咬指甲的习惯失败，感到灰心，熊爸爸和熊妈妈也为此感到沮丧。
[P27] 熊妈妈在家中打电话，向奶奶道谢，感谢她送的郁金香种子，表现出对当前困境的无奈与对生活的继续面对。
[P28] 熊妈妈打电话向奶奶请教如何帮助小熊妹妹改掉咬指甲的习惯，奶奶分享了自己小时候的经历，并建议用奖励金钱的方式，但要调整奖励的时机和方式。熊妈妈听后觉得这个主意非常好。
[P29] 熊妈妈和熊爸爸按照奶奶的建议，每天给小熊妹妹十枚硬币作为奖励，只要她不咬指甲就能保留，小熊妹妹带着硬币在上车和跳绳时都开心地听着硬币叮当响。
[P30] 小熊妹妹在尝试改掉咬指甲的习惯时，每当想咬指甲时，硬币叮当声会提醒她，这一招部分奏效。虽然她有时仍需归还硬币，但在十天内仍存下了九十三枚硬币。
[P31] 小熊妹妹成功改掉了咬指甲的习惯，拥有了漂亮的手指甲，并且在日常生活中能更自如地捡东西、调频道和挠痒痒，表现出习惯改变带来的积极变化。
[P32] 小熊妹妹通过抓石子游戏成功改掉咬指甲的习惯，父母为此感到欣慰，而小熊哥哥却羡慕地表示也要开始咬指甲以获得奖励。
[P33] 熊爸爸对小熊哥哥的玩笑表示愤怒，小熊哥哥连忙解释自己只是开玩笑，最终只能无奈地继续开玩笑。
[P34] 本页介绍了小熊妹妹在上学过程中逐渐养成咬指甲的习惯。她从幼儿园到一年级，因需要集中注意力而开始出现紧张的小动作，如咬指甲，最终导致指甲被咬得又短又疼。
[P35] 小熊妹妹因咬指甲被妈妈贴上胶带，虽然胶带提醒她不要咬指甲，但影响了日常活动，且在学校被同学嘲笑，最终她撕掉了胶带，但又忘记了不咬指甲。哥哥和妈妈都提醒她咬指甲是个坏习惯，妈妈提议带她去种郁金香时讨论‘习惯’是什么。
[P36] 本页讲述了小熊妹妹和妈妈讨论‘习惯’的概念，妈妈用推车在小路上压出深沟的比喻解释坏习惯难以戒除。爸爸提议用奖励（每天一毛钱）来帮助妹妹戒掉咬指甲的习惯，妹妹对此充满期待，但最终因未能坚持而感到沮丧。
[P37] 小熊妹妹在祖母的建议下，通过每天获得十枚硬币（每根指甲一枚）的奖励机制，成功戒掉了咬指甲的习惯。虽然过程中有反复，但十天后她攒了93枚硬币，并拥有了十根健康的指甲。哥哥开玩笑说也要开始咬指甲以获得奖励，爸爸生气地回应，哥哥连忙解释自己是在开玩笑。
[P38] 本页为绘本《坏习惯》的版权页，包含图书在版编目（CIP）数据、出版信息、版权说明、作者、译者、出版社、印刷信息及联系方式等。
